follow100Note: Snowflake spent $135.49 of every $100 it took in on direct and running costs — more than it earned — while other income added $6.72 and tax took $0.46, leaving a $29.24 loss per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Snowflake reports in thousands (revenue was $734,173K); figures here are shown in $M to three decimals so the lines foot exactly. Excluding stock-based pay and other non-GAAP items, operating income was $71.9M (a 10% margin). Chart note: Snowflake's running costs exceeded its gross profit by $260.6M, other income added $49.3M and tax took $3.4M, so the chart draws the remaining $214.7M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source.
oneTimers: $307.4M of stock-based compensation-related charges (including about $6.2M of employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions), excluded from non-GAAP results.
$22.5M of amortization of acquired intangibles, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
$2.7M of expenses associated with acquisitions and strategic investments, also excluded from non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income of $49.3M, net: $53.5M of interest income on Snowflake's cash and investments, partly offset by $4.2M of other expense, net. The income tax line was a $3.4M expense. Net loss attributable to Snowflake Inc. was $214.3M (EPS -$0.65), after $0.4M of loss attributable to noncontrolling interests.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers pay to store data and run computing and AI workloads on Snowflake's platform, billed by how much they use. Up 34% YoY and 95% of all revenue; product gross profit was $518.5M, a 74% margin.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Help getting set up and moving data onto Snowflake, plus other small items. Up 4% YoY — but it costs more to deliver than it brings in (a $13.3M gross loss).

sources.label: 10-Q for the quarter ended October 31, 2023 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 34% to $698.5M, the net revenue retention rate was 135%, and remaining performance obligations — work customers have already contracted — grew 23% to $3.7B. Snowflake guided Q4 FY24 product revenue to $716–$721M, up 29–30%, at a 4% non-GAAP operating margin, and full-year FY24 product revenue to $2,650M, up 37%.
takeaways.title: Product growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $260.6M, wider than the $206.0M loss a year ago. The main reason: $307.4M of stock-based compensation-related charges, including about $6.2M of employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions. Leaving those and similar items out, non-GAAP operating income was $71.9M, a 10% margin (up from 8% a year ago).
takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss, mostly stock pay

takeaways.text: Snowflake ended the quarter with 436 customers spending over $1M a year on the platform (+52% YoY) and 647 Forbes Global 2000 customers (+10% YoY). Operating cash flow was $120.9M, up 53% YoY, and adjusted free cash flow was $110.8M, up 70% YoY.
takeaways.title: Big customers kept spending

verdict: Snowflake's revenue grew 32% to $734.2M, with product revenue up 34% to $698.5M — but $307.4M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $260.6M and a net loss of $214.7M.
